content.text:
<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary below to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
I can't finish this rewrite yet. The summary has no years and no dates to calculate them from. The posting's one stated requirement is **8 years of backend engineering experience**, and I won't fill in a number that isn't in your material.

**How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?** A start year for your first backend role works too.

**What leaving it out costs:**
- **Automated filters.** Applicant tracking systems often screen on years of experience. A summary without a number may be filtered out before anyone reads it.
- **Recruiter skims.** Screeners check for the stated requirement first. With no number, they may assume you fall short, or move on rather than dig through your work history.
- **Weaker framing.** The 40,000-orders-a-day figure shows scale. Paired with years, it would also show sustained depth, which is what an 8-year requirement is screening for.
- **No way to show you exceed it.** If you have more than 8 years, the summary can't say so.

**Draft once you give me the figure:**

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and ran a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders a day. Earlier work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

**Fallback if you'd rather not state years:**

> Backend engineer specializing in transactional services. Most recently built and ran a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders a day. Earlier work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

This version doesn't address the requirement. It leaves the reader to work out your years from the dates in your work history, so those dates need to be clear and easy to find.
